<!-- pr-reviewer: ebfdbd34004d9f7f3a05079832d5046d3745b726 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge** (after PR 1464; retarget to main first).

Reviewed the 4-file delta against base `issue/1456-solidcraft-import`; built base+PR trial-merged with current main, locally (the diff against main carries 1464's Cargo.toml change, which the runner refuses).

## What looks good
- Vertex check sits right after `native::decode` and before anything reaches the kernel (`cache.rs` `check_vertices`): non-finite and past 1e6 mm refused, vertex index and limit named. No unwrap/expect/panic, no new dependency, files well under 400 lines, provenance line present, decisions file with chosen/why/dropped, body has `Changelog:`, `Fixes`, stacking stated.
- The hostile test rewrites the slice table, both SHA-256 digests and CRCs, so the body decoder is really reached; the damaged-body test fails any refusal that does not name the final body, so a container-level rejection fails it. The 120 s bound runs through `bounded_cancel` with a cancel token (a real guard, though a hung decoder call itself would only be cut at the next case boundary).

## Results (trial merge with main, local, debug)
- `cargo test -p camcraft-kernel --test solidcraft_hostile --test solidcraft_import`: 3 + 7 pass (damaged bodies: 6 still import, 0 panics).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Old code check (base `cache.rs` under the new test): `hostile_coordinates_are_refused_by_name` FAILS (the 1e9 case was already refused, at `measure`, but not by name: "not a positive finite solid measure"). The damaged-body and deflate tests pass on the old code: they are regression pins, not fixes.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. Still unchecked by the reader: surface and curve parameters (normals, axes, origins, transforms) and edge/face indices; only vertex points get the 1e6 mm bound. I rely on the decoder's own finite/1e12 checks for those, which I did not audit. Worth a follow-up issue if any of those reach the kernel unvalidated.
2. "non-finite metadata" for 1e13 does mildly mislead (the value is finite, just past the decoder's 1e12). Not unsafe; a one-line note in the decisions file or a wrapper of the message would help.
3. The limit is stated, named in the error and in the decisions file; the 1e6 mm check applies per axis, which the doc comment says.
4. Not exercised: Linux/macOS; the 24-case fuzz is a fixed seed, so coverage is narrow.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
